column1: Since March, real activity remains solid and the labor market strong, while inflation runs below 2%. The FOMC held the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent and maintained patient guidance, alongside a technical IOER adjustment consistent with operating a floor system. Beige Book reports from March–April indicate modest growth across Districts: consumer spending at general retailers and auto dealers was mixed/soft, manufacturing expanded modestly amid trade-related uncertainty, and agricultural conditions were pressured by heavy rainfall and flooding; labor markets stayed tight and price pressures muted. The April SLOOS showed tighter standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and softer demand for several consumer credit categories, pointing to a modestly more restrictive credit environment. Together with financial stability concerns about somewhat elevated valuations and high business debt vulnerabilities, the balance of risks is more balanced with mild downside tilt despite strong labor data. sentiment score = 0.05
